shorts.title: Why You Should Never Sit Under the Manchineel in the Rain
shorts.outro: Doug sat under it anyway. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Guinness World Records lists the manchineel as the most dangerous tree in the world, and rain dripping off its leaves can carry blistering sap onto anyone sheltering underneath. Doug sat there anyway. The science is real and sourced in the full video.

shorts.hook: California lines its highways with twenty-five million poisonous shrubs.
shorts.title: Two Scientists Tested the Oleander Hot Dog Story
shorts.outro: Doug's other four deaths are in the full video below.
shorts.description: In 2020 two toxicologists roasted hot dogs on oleander sticks and found only a negligible amount of toxin, but the leaves are another matter. Doug's cartoon death and his other four are in the full video.

shorts.hook: Researchers call this one of the most venomous plants in the world.
shorts.title: This Plant Can Still Sting a Hundred Years After It Dies
shorts.outro: Doug survived. His other five deaths are in the full video.
shorts.description: The gympie-gympie's silica hairs inject a venom that University of Queensland researchers compare to spider and cone snail toxins, and dried specimens over a century old can still sting. Doug survived; the sources are in the full video.
